**John Levendis**

*Economics Bulletin* 45(4), 1915–1925, 2025

The Arellano-Bond type dynamic panel estimators are known to suffer from over-instrumentation. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we compare Difference and System GMM with both default and collapsed instrument sets across varying numbers of countries and time periods typical in macroeconomic analysis. Collapsing consistently outperforms default instrumentation, providing more accurate estimates, especially as T increases. System GMM with collapsed instruments performs best overall, especially for endogenous variables. These findings strongly support using collapsed instruments for the analysis of macroeconomic panels, regardless of the number of countries or time periods.

[PDF](../files/Levendis2025default.pdf)

### Why This Research Matters

The Arellano-Bond family of dynamic panel estimators are workhorses of empirical macroeconomics and finance. But they have a well-known weakness: the number of internally generated instruments grows quadratically with the number of time periods. Too many instruments overfit the endogenous variables, bias estimates toward OLS, and render diagnostic tests useless.

Collapsing the instrument matrix reduces instrument growth from quadratic to linear in T. It is available as a simple option in standard software, but many researchers stick with the default, and no study had systematically compared the two across sample sizes typical in macroeconomic research.

### What I Found

**Collapsed instruments outperform default instruments in virtually every configuration.** Across Monte Carlo simulations spanning N=10 to 200 countries and T=20 to 50 periods, collapsing produces more accurate point estimates and smaller standard errors for all three parameters tested: the autoregressive coefficient, an exogenous variable, and an endogenous variable.

**System GMM with collapsed instruments is the best overall performer.** It recovers the true autoregressive parameter (0.70) most accurately — estimates hover around 0.71 across all sample sizes — while difference GMM with default instruments shows severe downward bias that worsens as T grows (as low as 0.572 with N=10, T=50).

**The advantage of collapsing grows with T.** Default instruments grow as roughly ½pT² while collapsed instruments grow as pT. The longer the panel, the worse the overfitting problem, and the greater the benefit of collapsing.

### Implications

Use system GMM with collapsed instruments as the default for dynamic panel estimation. There is no configuration in these simulations where default instruments outperform collapsed ones. Researchers who report only default-instrument results — which remains common practice — are likely reporting less accurate estimates with inflated precision.
